blocks.value: A thread is the smallest unit of execution the operating system can schedule. A process is a group of threads running together in the same shared environment. A single-threaded process has exactly one thread; a multithreaded process has more than one, and those threads share the same memory space so they can communicate directly.

Concurrency is the property of running multiple threads and processes at the same time. An OS thread scheduler decides which threads run when. If a thread's allotted time runs out before it finishes, a context switch happens: its current state is saved so it can be resumed later exactly where it left off.

Every Java application already runs on one thread automatically: the main thread, created by the JVM to execute main(). You can create and start additional threads to run parts of your program in parallel with it.
